title: Prove terminal attach in Node Vitest

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: one scratch break check

Verdict: Caught

Story and revision
- Story: .planning/seeds/SEED-413-renovate-dashboard-unit-tests.md#prove-terminal-attach-and-cursor-turns-on-vitest ("Prove terminal attach in Node Vitest"), plan .planning/slice-plans/871-prove-terminal-attach-on-vitest/PLAN.md.
- Revision: 4d6c77cadc8fd8b27ecc9f5fb2168f7710061bbc (claude/prove-terminal-attach-in-node-vitest).
- Promise: "Given saved Codex context, opening the terminal resumes that conversation on its recorded remote transport". The part checked: the resumed Codex PTY gets the developer's shell environment, not the dashboard deployment's start-up environment.

Fault (the caller's suggestion, used unchanged)
- dashboard/server/hosts/codex/terminal.ts line 36: changed `env: developerShellEnvironment(process.env),` to `env: { ...process.env } as Record<string, string>,`. No fixture or assertion was changed.

Assertion examined (the caller's suggestion, used unchanged)
- dashboard/backend-tests/terminals/agent-terminal-codex.spec.ts:99, "saved context supplies native resume, transport and detach without replay or fork". The check at lines 123-128 is `expect(developerShellViolations(resumes.at(-1), fakeCodexHost("FAKE_CODEX_TERMINAL_ROOT"))).toEqual([])`. The fixture is the spec's own beforeAll: `deploymentLikeStart` from test-support/support/launchEnvironment.ts adds deployment-like PATH entries, npm_* variables, INIT_CWD and DOUGH_SPEC_PASSTHROUGH to process.env before the terminal boundary starts.

Runs (isolated scratch worktree at the selected revision, after npm ci; the command was the caller's, with a fresh proof-record path for each run)
- Pre-probe state: clean (`git status --porcelain` showed 0 entries).
- Baseline: 3 of 3 tests passed (duration 9.83s). The case at :99 ran (595ms), so its environment assertion ran on a recorded resume environment.
- Faulted: the case at :99 failed at line 128 with "expected [ …(33) ] to deeply equal []". The other 2 cases passed. afterAll then timed out after 10000ms, because the failed case never closed its terminal. That is a side effect of the failure, not a second catch.
- Reach and wrong behavior: the violations come from the environment that the fake `codex` recorded for the resume PTY (`codexEnvironments(native, "resume")`, exactly one resume). The resumed process actually received the start-up environment:
  - 20 npm_* variables, including npm_lifecycle_event and npm_config_local_prefix from the fixture
  - NODE_ENV and INIT_CWD
  - the fixture's deployment PATH entries `/var/folders/.../dough-deployment-S1oFf7/node_modules/@npmcli/run-script/lib/node-gyp-bin` and `.../node_modules/.bin`, plus npm's own node_modules/.bin and node-gyp-bin entries

  So the wrong behavior was seen on the promised path (attach leading to `codex resume --remote`), and the maintained assertion is the one that failed on it.
- Restoration: a shell EXIT trap ran `git checkout -- dashboard/server/hosts/codex/terminal.ts`. Afterwards `git status --porcelain` showed 0 entries and HEAD was still 4d6c77cad. The same command was rerun and passed 3 of 3 (duration 9.05s).
- Cleanup: the afterAll timeout in the faulted run left one orphaned scratch process: `dashboard/server/hosts/cursor/runnerMain.ts`, PID 50742, parent PID 1, started 09:46:59 during the faulted run. It was killed. The scratch worktree was then removed (`git worktree remove --force`). The execution worktree was not touched and is still clean.

Claim limit: the catch covers the Codex native-resume attach path when started under the spec's deployment-like start-up. It says nothing about other hosts' launch environments.

Next proof action: none needed for this promise. The restored `developerShellViolations` assertion is not vacuous; this probe now shows that by a run, not only by code reading.

Prior disposition: this result matches the execution's own claim that the restored check is non-vacuous. Execution had shown that only by reading the code; this probe confirms it with a faulted run. No new repair decision comes from the probe. A separate observation, not part of the verdict: when this case fails, afterAll times out and can orphan a cursor runner process. The caller decides whether that matters.

Cost
- Test runtime (measured, Vitest "Duration" per run): baseline 9.83s, faulted roughly 10s of tests plus the 10s afterAll timeout (exact total not captured), restored 9.05s. That is about 39s across the three runs. npm ci time was not measured separately.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part in this invocation.
- Agent effort: unavailable. This agent has no token or step meter; it made about 10 tool calls (estimated count).


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 111132 ms (measured), from 1795743967000 to 1795744078132 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition: 4d6c77cadc8fd8b27ecc9f5fb2168f7710061bbc, Caught, no follow-up.
